page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.4-16 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured within the Standard instance family. It is powered by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor platform using the 64-bit arm64 instruction set architecture. The instance allocates 8 dedicated physical cores operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. Because each core runs a single execution thread with one thread per core, applications run without the resource contention typical of simultaneous multithreading environments.

The instance includes 16.0 GB of system RAM, providing an allocation of 2.0 GB per physical core. This shape contains no local NVMe storage, meaning persistent disk operations require network-attached storage volumes. In addition, the configuration features no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for external ingress and egress traffic.

With its 1:2 core-to-memory allocation, VM.Standard.A4.Flex.4-16 provides a balanced profile for compute-oriented tasks. It delivers favorable cost efficiency per execution core for distributed workloads compiled for ARM architecture, including CI/CD build environments, containerized microservices, API servers, and scalable web application backends. Tasks requiring high memory footprints per thread or large local disk caches will require alternative configurations.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.4-16 is an ARM-based compute instance built on the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor architecture. The server provides 8 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.6 GHz, featuring a single hardware thread per core with dedicated allocation. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not package integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators. With its 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, this shape provides predictable compute performance across all allocated execution units. VM.Standard.A4.Flex.4-16 is well configured for ARM-native software builds, distributed containerized workloads, continuous integration workers, and general compute-driven backend services.
